Prosecutors are reopening a Cornell fraternity rape case. Here's what we know

New York prosecutors are reopening an investigation into an alleged rape case at Cornell University in 2024. The alleged victim recently filed a lawsuit against seven members of Chi Phi fraternity.

Actual Article Body:
Jaclyn Diaz

People walk on the campus of Cornell University in Ithaca, N.Y., in 2024.
                
                    
                    Seth Wenig/AP
                    
                
                hide caption

New York prosecutors say they are reopening an investigation into an alleged rape case from 2024 that involved Cornell University students.

This comes after the alleged victim, referred to as Jane Doe, filed a lawsuit in the Supreme Court of the State of New York this month. In it, she claims multiple men drugged and brutally raped her for more than four hours at Cornell's Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Amendment 81: Colorado police, prosecutors would be forced to alert ICE after filing certain charges

The ballot measure would require police and prosecutors to notify the Department of Homeland Security when someone living in the U.S. illegally, or with uncertain immigrant status, is charged with a violent crime or if they’ve been previously convicted of a felony

Actual Article Body:
The Colorado Sun

Telling stories that matter in a dynamic, evolving state.

Colorado voters will decide in November whether to require state and local law enforcement to work more closely with federal immigration authorities.

Amendment 81, brought by a conservative political group, would require police and prosecutors to notify the U.S. Department of Homeland Security when someone who is living in the U.S. illegally is charged with certain crimes.

Read on for more on what the initiative would do, who is behind it and who is opposing it.

Amendment 81 would amend the state constitution to require that police officers, sheriff’s deputies and prosecutors alert the U.S. Department of Homeland Security if they formally charge someone whose immigration status is in question
